summary: Dependency-confusion payload exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via native addon on require()
details: The package presents a benign NestJS commons wrapper (index.js exports forRoot/createLogger) but on require() loads prebuilds/linux-x64/metrics.node inside a swallowed try/catch. The bundled Linux ELF reads CI and cloud credential environment variables (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and other AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN) along with host identifiers from gethostname/getpwuid/getcwd/uname and POSTs them in cleartext HTTP to the hardcoded external host oob.s4yhii.com with payload tagged "src":"native". The addon fork+setsid's to persist independently of the loading process. The package name sits in an @galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20-lite scope with version 999.0.1, a dependency-confusion shape designed to win resolution against an internal package of the same name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
